A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Skyfall-GS and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite substantial reformatting and supplementary additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original DFC2019 and GoogleEarth experiments, component ablations, qualitative reconstructions, and two user studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional geometry validation, refinement ablations, scalability experiments, and qualitative robustness analyses.

M1.justification: Equation 3 changes the stated depth objective from |PCorr| to 1 - |PCorr|, correcting its optimization direction. The reconstruction-plus-curriculum-refinement pipeline otherwise remains intact. This establishes a written objective correction, without establishing whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: The original DFC2019 and GoogleEarth scene coverage is retained, including v1's additional Jacksonville AOIs. v2 adds Neuschwanstein Castle and Wells Cathedral examples and jointly reconstructs adjacent JAX_214/JAX_260 blocks, extending architectural and spatial-scale coverage within the existing synthesis task.

E2.justification: v2 adds Mip-Splatting to the reported GoogleEarth comparisons, DFC2019 per-scene table, and both user studies. Although v1 already mentions evaluating it on both datasets, these corresponding comparisons omit it. Table 4 also introduces an evaluated SDEdit replacement control; the established comparator suite is otherwise retained.

E3.justification: The reported user-study cohort changes from 89 to 44 participants per study, with expanded comparator choices. New protocols include LiDAR-based DSM evaluation using MAE/RMSE, matched-schedule SDEdit testing, and multi-block training with a 6-by-3 look-at grid. Appendix B.1 also specifies disabling GoogleEarth opacity regularization, revising v1's unqualified regularization setting without establishing whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 extend perceptual ablations with geometric validation, sample counts of 1/2/3/5, timing, prompt controls, and SDEdit replacement. Appendix D adds prompt sensitivity, transient-object handling, bridge and irregular-geometry cases, multi-block consistency, episode-versus-coverage analysis, and seed-dependent appearance comparisons. These substantially broaden tests of mechanisms, robustness, and applicability.

E5.justification: Appendix D and Figure 23 newly report varying diffusion random seeds while holding geometric initialization fixed. This adds qualitative seed-sensitivity information; neither version supplies quantitative uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the main comparisons.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, 8, and 9 revise numerous scores: Skyfall-GS FIDCLIP changes from 27.35 to 27.03 on DFC2019 and 9.91 to 10.29 on GoogleEarth. User-study percentages are replaced under changed study conditions. New results include reconstruction MAE/RMSE of 2.250/3.483 meters, refinement-control results, coverage curves, and scalability findings; these are additions or revisions, not uniformly comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 3 corrects the mathematical definition of the depth loss to 1 - |PCorr|. Appendix B.2 additionally states the weak-perspective assumption Z much greater than depth variation and explains the projection-matrix approximation. No substantial theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The satellite-only, domain-independent, curriculum-refinement contribution remains. v2 recasts the abstract/introduction's broad priority wording as a hybrid reconstruction-and-generation framework while retaining qualified first-method claims elsewhere. Its conclusion additionally claims operation without human intervention.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning fixed-camera blind spots, dependence on off-nadir imagery, and coverage estimates that cannot detect missing surfaces. It interprets weaker performance on relatively flat scenes, discusses competing LPIPS/SSIM results, and explains prompt robustness, transient-object handling, and seed-dependent textures. These substantially expand the applicability boundaries and mechanism discussion beyond v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents appearance fusion for standard renderers, memory and Gaussian counts, detailed runtime profiling, approximation procedures, prompt variants, and multi-block settings. Conversely, it omits v1's densification-threshold and extended CoR-GS-training details, Zenodo example-data notice, and code/full-data release promises. These are substantial documentation changes; actual external resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises positioning around satellite reconstruction, urban synthesis, and diffusion editing. It adds works including Horizon-GS, Sat2City, Sat3DGen, Sat2RealCity, WonderWorld, and RealmDreamer, while removing some earlier citations. New comparisons emphasize preserving observed facade appearance versus unconstrained inpainting, beyond bibliographic or citation-style changes.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, experimental discussion, and conclusion receive substantial rewriting. The appendix is reorganized into implementation, main-experiment details, and additional experiments; performance/scalability gains a dedicated subsection. The ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-disclosure sections are removed. This extends well beyond renumbering or added scientific content alone.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different page format, expands ablation tables, adds ranking colors and comparator columns, and redraws the user-study charts. New figures display refinement progression, scalability, complex geometry, prompts, embeddings, coverage, and seed variation. The earlier pseudo-camera sampling scatterplot is removed, while many original figures are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the paper's central geometric and refinement claims through LiDAR validation, SDEdit and sample-count controls, and multi-block/coverage analyses. It also corrects the depth objective and states concrete applicability limits. These gains outweigh lost reproducibility disclosures and remaining reporting problems: notably, Section C.3 claims three GoogleEarth CMMD wins, whereas Table 9 shows two. The improvement rests on better validation and qualification, not higher scores or greater length.
